div.head: Annexe II

list.label: a.
list.item: A State whose nationals are engaged “on the High Seas” in fishing “any stock of fish not being fished by” nationals of other States, may regulate and control fishing activities for “that stock” for the purpose of “making possible the maximum sustained yield from that stock.”
list.label: b.
list.item: If the nationals of two or more States are engaged in fishing “the same stock of fish” the States concerned shall prescribe the necessary measures by agreement.
list.label: c.
list.item:
If subsequent to the adoption “and application” of such measures the nationals of other States (“desire” to) engage in fishing for these stocks, they shall observe the measures in effect. Provided however that if the concerned stock reasonably fulfils the following conditions: (1)
It is the subject of scientific research for the purpose of determining measures necessary for making possible the maximum sustained yield. (2)
It is under regulations for the same purpose. (3)
Any further increase in fishing would not result in any substantial increase in sustained yield; the other States will abstain from fishing that stock.
list.label: d.
list.item: In the event that agreement is not reached regarding the measures referred to in 1 b., or if the other States referred to in 1 c. do not agree with the measures in force, or if there is disagreement as to whether a stock reasonably fulfils all the conditions for abstention listed in 1 c., the question shall, at the request of one of the interested parties, be referred to the international body envisaged in Article 3.
list.label: e.
list.item:
None of the provisions of this Article shall be construed as preventing 1)
A State from regulating its nationals for any purpose;
2)
Two or more States by agreement from regulating their nationals for any purpose.

div.p: With respect to any stock of fish in waters contiguous to the territorial waters of a coastal State, the coastal State is entitled to take part on an equal footing in any system or agreement for the purpose of research on and regulation of that stock, even though its nationals do not carry on fishing for that stock, (provided that participation in regulation shall be contingent upon participation in any programme of research.)

States shall be under duty to accept the decisions of the international authority defined below with respect to the questions referred to it under Article 1 preceding. The international authority shall be constituted as follows:

If a State or States questions the qualifications for abstention or the measures in effect, the questioning State or States shall appoint one arbitrator, the regulating State or States shall appoint one arbitrator, and the two arbitrators shall appoint a third arbitrator.

In the event that the first two arbitrators are unable to agree within one month upon the third arbitrator, such third arbitrator shall be appointed by the President of the International Court of Justice. In the event that either the challenging State or States or the regulating State or States, shall have failed to appoint an arbitrator within one month at being notified of the appointment of the arbitrator of the other side, the President of the International Court of Justice shall appoint such arbitrator.

Questions to be determined by the arbitral tribunal shall be limited to the following: 1.
With respect to abstentions: a.
Does the stock of fish reasonably satisfy the following: 1.
Is the stock subject to reasonably adequate scientific investigation with the objective of determining measures required to make possible the maximum sustained yield. 2.
Is the stock under regulation for the purpose of making possible the maximum sustained yield. 3.
Is the stock under such exploitation that an increase in the amount of fishing will not result in a substantial sustained increase in yield.
2.
With respect to conservation measures:
a.
Are the regulations based on appropriate scientific findings. b.
Are the regulations necessary to make possible the maximum sustained yield. c.
Are the regulations reasonable. d.
Are the regulations designed to, or in fact do they, discriminate against any State.
[Here follow draft articles for a general multilateral fishery regulation convention proposed by the United Kingdom.]
